fields.rules: conventions for the spoken text that a lookup cannot apply (numbers, dates, pauses, names)
fields.asr_aliases: Whisper QA only: map both the reference and the transcript through these before the word-error rate; never used to write spoken text

Engine: the engine the item was observed with; kokoro is the channel's primary (guide §5), and an item for another engine is a lead to test, not a rule

rules.rule: Write abbreviations without periods in the spoken text, and scan the spoken text for a single letter followed by '. ' before synthesis.
rules.why: Kokoro pauses about 0.3 s at the periods of 'A.I.' even in one call, and a splitter at '. ' cuts the sentence there too; Whisper on the mix heard 'an A model' and passed it
rules.source: v013-jev-decisions/plan/plan.md:313-317; v013-jev-decisions/tools/synth_kokoro.py:110; v012-black-hole-jets/tools/synth_kokoro.py:61; v900-qft/v3/synth_cb.py:76; raibo2-marathon/tools/make_vo.py:57; RS-ENGINE-PRODUCTION-GUIDE.md:580; probe 2026-09-30 (kokoro-onnx v1.0, af_heart, Whisper large-v3)

rules.rule: Replace an en dash with 'to' only between numbers; elsewhere use a hyphen or a space.
rules.example: '40–70 percent' -> 'forty to seventy percent', but 'Harvard–Smithsonian' -> 'Harvard-Smithsonian'
rules.why: make_vo_en.spoken() replaces every '–' with ' to '. The published narration therefore says 'Harvard to Smithsonian'. v900 synth_cb.spoken() has the same blanket replace. It is latent there, because the current v900 script has no en dash. Piper make_audio.py mapped it to a space and re-hyphenated the name.

rules.rule: Replace an em dash with a comma pause.
rules.why: Both Chatterbox pipelines do this before synthesis.

rules.rule: Strip curly quotes and quote marks around a mentioned word; say the word plain.
rules.example: “plink” -> plink; ‘wind’ -> wind
rules.why: Piper's spoken() strips them. The Chatterbox pass left curly quotes in, and Whisper still heard the lines (WER 0.03-0.05 came from names).

rules.rule: Turn a colon into a full stop in the spoken text where a real pause is wanted; the caption keeps the colon.
rules.example: 'Four steps, nonstop:' -> 'Four steps, nonstop.'; 'free order is ahead: forty-one percent' -> 'free order is ahead. Forty-one percent, against thirty-five.'
rules.why: The pause comes from the sentence break (Piper's sentence-silence, Kokoro's per-sentence takes).

rules.rule: Add commas for prosody: around a word that is mentioned rather than used, before a coined term, and after a long numeric subject.
rules.example: 'Words like, therefore, thus, and since, are forks'; 'The authors call this, entropy degradation.'; 'Zero point zero two, means two percent'
rules.why: Kokoro otherwise runs the mention into the sentence. The written text keeps normal punctuation.

rules.rule: Do not put a parenthetical acronym after its expansion in the spoken text.
rules.example: 'Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU)' -> spoken without '(ONU)'
rules.why: The caption keeps it (pt-BR case; the rule is language-neutral).

rules.rule: Give a single capital letter a noun, or spell its letter name, so that it is not read as a word or joined to its neighbour.
rules.example: 'from A to B' -> 'from point ay, to point bee'; 'A' -> 'the potential A'
rules.why: Bare letters are ambiguous. 'queue A or queue B' is still heard 'QA/QO or QB' (v013 text.value 0.13, the only beat over the gate).

rules.rule: Kokoro reads common initialisms as letters, and acronyms that are words as words, without help: test a new one with tools/vo_probe.py and record it here (spoken = written when it reads correctly). Spell letters with spaces (R L H F) only where a test shows a wrong reading, and for Piper; keep a pronounceable acronym as a word, with a hyphenated respelling if needed (Low-far).
rules.example: RLHF, LLMs, GPT, JSON, HTTP, FAQ, CUDA, NVIDIA: read correctly as written by af_heart
rules.why: v013 and flexibility-trap spaced initialisms as a precaution; the probe shows it is not needed for Kokoro

rules.rule: Split CamelCase and hyphenated product names into words.
rules.example: HumanEval -> Human Eval; JustGRPO -> Just G R P O; jev-latest -> Jev latest; MATH-500 -> Math 500
rules.why: Kokoro reads run-together names unpredictably (inferred from the respellings chosen).

rules.rule: A respelling lives in the spoken form only (SPOKEN / SPOKEN_BEAT / tts / spoken field). The caption keeps the written form.
rules.example: SPOKEN_BEAT['launch'] vs ACTS text
rules.why: A single source of truth drives voice, captions and scene. Word timings are mapped back to the written words.

rules.rule: Word-level respelling maps must list every inflected form and are case-sensitive.
rules.example: 'Dirac' and 'Dirac's' both mapped; 'Faraday's' mapped but not 'Faraday'
rules.why: v900 spoken() replaces whole [A-Za-z']+ tokens by exact dictionary lookup. A capitalised sentence-initial 'Gluons' would not match (inferred).

rules.rule: Key spoken-form overrides by act and beat, or keep beat ids unique across acts.
rules.example: v013 has beat 'state' in both 'inout' and 'limits'
rules.why: SPOKEN_BEAT is keyed by beat id alone, so a respelling for one 'state' would silently apply to the other (inferred). The synthesis report already collided on this id.

rules.rule: Years: use the year form. Put years and dense numbers on screen rather than speaking them in full where the shot is short.
rules.example: 2024 -> twenty twenty-four; 1933 -> nineteen thirty-three
rules.why: num2words(to='year'). The default num2words(2024) gives 'two thousand and twenty-four', a residual WER source in raibo2's gate (tested on a copy of the function).

rules.rule: Dates: the day is an ordinal.
rules.example: September 15 -> September fifteenth
rules.why: A cardinal day would be read 'September fifteen'.

rules.rule: Decimals: say 'point', then each digit. Say 'zero' before a leading decimal point. Say a round fraction as a word where natural.
rules.example: 0.25 -> zero point two five; 45.5 -> forty-five point five; 0.5 -> half; 0.3 mm -> a third of a millimetre
rules.why: Matches the v013 gate normaliser, which reads fractional digits one by one.

rules.rule: Versions: each dot is 'point' and each part is a whole number.
rules.example: 1.13.0 -> one point thirteen point zero; GPT-5.6 -> G P T five point six
rules.why: Only multi-dot numbers get this treatment in the normaliser.

rules.rule: Four-digit quantities are read in hundreds. Drop the thousands separator.
rules.example: 1,250 -> twelve hundred and fifty; 1,280 -> twelve hundred and eighty; 10,000 -> ten thousand
rules.why: The generic digit regexes break on ',' (see the next rule).

rules.rule: Never feed digits with separators to a number regex that does not know the locale. Pre-spell them in the spoken text.
rules.example: EN port of the pt words(): '1,250' -> 'one,two hundred and fifty', '0.250' -> 'two hundred and fifty', '2.5' -> 'two.five'; beta-pic generic pass: '1,250' -> 'one,two hundred and fifty' unless NAMES catches it
rules.why: Tested on copies of the functions in the scratchpad. v010's short make_vo_chatterbox.py is the pt-BR script with lang='en', and it keeps '.' as the thousands separator. It is latent there, because the Short's lines have no digits.

rules.rule: Say percent as 'percent'. Say a numeric range as 'X to Y'. In a pair of percentages the second may drop 'percent'.
rules.example: 40 % -> forty percent; 40–70 % -> forty to seventy percent; 83% ... 67% -> eighty-three percent ... sixty-seven
rules.why: Gate normalisers map '%' to 'percent'.

rules.rule: Say multipliers as 'N times'. The gate maps '×' to 'times'.
rules.example: 3× -> three times; 193.6 times

rules.rule: Expand units and symbols to words. A unit may be simplified to its meaning.
rules.example: m/s -> metres per second; km -> kilometres; ° -> degrees; °C -> degrees; lbf -> pounds of thrust; kHz -> kilohertz; mm -> millimetre; δ -> delta
rules.why: Engines read symbols and unit abbreviations unreliably (inferred from every project spelling them out).

rules.rule: Spell out numbers in the spoken form for every engine. Captions keep digits.
rules.example: 'Numbers are spelled for the voice and written in the captions.'
rules.why: Kokoro misreads digit decimals and versions and pauses inside them (67.8% heard as '67, 8%', 1.13.0 left a 0.49 s pause)
rules.source: raibo2-marathon/tools/script.py:4; v003-jet-engine/publish/make_audio.py:8; v008-bubble-sound/tools/script.py:4; v012-black-hole-jets/script/narration.py:4; beta-pic-b-radio/publish/make_vo_en.py:42; probe 2026-09-30 (kokoro-onnx v1.0, af_heart, Whisper large-v3)

rules.rule: Numbers on screen only when spoken, and on the word that names them.
rules.example: counter keyed to the spoken number's word
rules.why: Guide density rule.

rules.rule: Kokoro: one sentence per call, one take per sentence. Fix a bad reading by changing the text (respelling, punctuation, splitting), never by re-rolling.
rules.example: WER_MAX fail -> edit SPOKEN_BEAT
rules.why: Kokoro is deterministic.

rules.rule: Chatterbox: never synthesise a sentence under 7 words alone. Merge it with its neighbour, and cut the take at the script's last word (not Whisper's last word).
rules.example: 'This is the principle of equivalence.' then babble
rules.why: Chatterbox babbles after short standalone sentences. raibo2's make_vo.py splits at [.?!:] and voices pieces as short as 2-3 words ('Without that reward:', 'Passed twice.', 'Back to Sangju.') cut at Whisper's last word. That is the risk pattern, though raibo2 passed its gate (inferred latent).

rules.rule: Voice a list of single words as one connected take, not one take per word.
rules.example: 'Suck, squeeze, bang, blow!' as one take at length-scale 1.25, word onsets measured from the take
rules.why: Single-word Piper takes come out clipped.

rules.rule: Cut every take at its recognised words: about 0.10-0.15 s before the first and 0.22-0.25 s after the last. Allow a longer tail (0.45 s) when a line ends on a number.
rules.example: HEAD, TAIL = 0.12, 0.25; TAIL_S = 0.45
rules.why: This removes Chatterbox run-on (breaths, mumbles). Whisper ends a spoken number early.

rules.rule: Put pauses in the assembly, not in the text: fixed silences between sentences of a beat, between beats, and extra after a full stop.
rules.example: v013 INNER 0.38 / GAP 0.55 + SENTENCE 0.45; v012 0.55 / 0.6 + 0.5; v900 synth_cb INNER 0.42 / GAP 0.5 + 0.45; raibo2 PAUSE 0.34 after a full stop, 0.26 after a colon
rules.why: Guide §14.

rules.rule: Leave longer gaps at movement or chapter changes and a breath before key reveals. Leave 1-2 s without narration before big reveals.
rules.example: raibo2 GAP_DEFAULT 0.7, GAP_MOVEMENT 2.6, GAP_EXTRA up to 1.2 s

rules.rule: Pace: 4.5-6 syllables/s and at most 2.8 words/s. Calm, well-reviewed films run 95-120 words/min. Never time-compress. Ease a fast take by at most 15 % with formant-preserving rubberband.
rules.example: raibo2 eased to 4.6 syll/s (MAX_EASE 0.86); v012 speed 0.88 for <= 2.8 w/s; v013 133 wpm with pauses
rules.why: Rushed delivery (7-9 syllables/s) and compression artefacts passed a word-error check.

rules.rule: Measure pace as words (or syllables) over the clip duration, not over Whisper's first-to-last-word span. Vowel-group syllable counting over-counts English; raibo2 subtracts a silent final 'e'.
rules.example: beta-pic: PACE 2.7 / FAST 3.1 words/s; v900: PACE 2.9 / FAST 3.3; v010 Short: 4.2-4.4 vowel groups/s
rules.why: Whisper's span overstates pace.

rules.rule: For timing estimates before synthesis, count numbers and acronyms as the words they are spoken as.
rules.why: Slot lengths were computed from the text before any audio existed.

rules.rule: In shorts, keep one line per shot that ends before the cut. Shorten the lines rather than speeding them up.
rules.example: v010 Short: 8 takes, VO_MAX_STRETCH=1.0, VO_CFG=0.3, eased to 4.4

rules.rule: Gate every line with Whisper large-v3 on the final mix (not only the raw take). Kokoro WER_MAX is 0.12 (v013) or 0.15 (v012); the Chatterbox vo_qa flags above 0.08.
rules.example: qa/vo_qa.py out/film.mp4
rules.why: Guide gate.

rules.rule: Score WER against a normalised form that folds formatting (years, %, ×, ordinals, decimals, versions, 'a hundred', dropped 'and', joined spelled letters) and maps every respelling back through an alias table. Otherwise respellings read as errors and real errors hide in the noise.
rules.example: v900 per-take WER against 'glue-ons' was 0.278 though Whisper heard 'gluons'; v013 ALIAS archive->arxiv, nowl->noul
rules.why: v900 synth_cb scores against the respelled text with no alias map. beta-pic scores against the written text.

rules.rule: A word Whisper drops or truncates in the mix is a listening cue, not an ASR quirk. Have a person listen to the opening line.
rules.example: 'an A model' (WER 0.10) was the A.I. split, first put down to transcription

rules.rule: Fold British and American spellings in the gate. Whisper writes American forms.
rules.example: centre/center, metres/meters, kilometres/kilometers, colour/color, modelled/modeled, travelling/traveling, disc/disk
rules.why: Only v012 (disc->disk) and v900 shorts (color->colour) fold any. The others show up as residual WER.

rules.rule: Run vo.hazards on every spoken line before synthesis, then have a person listen to the opening line; Whisper on the mix can mis-hear a split word as a plausible one and pass it.
rules.example: Whisper heard 'an A model' for 'an A... I model'

rules.rule: Hyphenated identifiers (model tags, handles) lose the hyphen and are written as the words they are said as.
rules.example: jev-latest -> Jev latest

rules.rule: Write money as words with the unit last in the spoken text. In the word-error check, pass both sides through vo.asr_currency() before spelling the numbers.
rules.example: '$11.6 billion' -> 'eleven point six billion dollars'; a transcript's '$450 billion' -> '450 billion dollars'
rules.why: Whisper writes the symbol first ('$450 billion') for a narration that says 'four hundred fifty billion dollars'; a normaliser that only drops the symbol loses the word 'dollars' and scores a false error on every figure
rules.source: v015-short-pack s18 and s19 (tools/vo_core.py norm); Whisper large-v3 on Kokoro af_heart, 2026-10-01

rules.rule: Spell every number as words before Chatterbox. Years are pt-BR cardinals.
rules.example: 1933 -> mil novecentos e trinta e três
rules.why: Chatterbox reads digits unreliably. Years came out as 1983/1993 before this rule. 'Numbers are read as words, so years come out correctly.'

rules.rule: Ordinals: 'Nº' becomes ordinal words.
rules.example: 1º -> primeiro; 6º -> sexto
rules.why: num2words(to='ordinal', lang='pt_BR').

rules.rule: Thousands separator is '.': read the group as one number.
rules.example: 5.772 -> cinco mil setecentos e setenta e dois

rules.rule: Decimal comma is spoken 'vírgula'. Pre-spell decimals in the spoken text, because the synthesis-side words() does not handle them.
rules.example: 1,4 -> um vírgula quatro; 0,7 % -> zero vírgula sete por cento
rules.why: words() turns '1,4' into 'um,quatro' and '0,7 %' into 'zero,sete %' (tested on a copy). Only vo_qa.to_words handles the comma, and make_vo's WER still counted Whisper's '1,4'/'0,7%' as errors (0.062/0.176).

rules.rule: Percent is 'por cento'.
rules.example: 0,7 % -> zero vírgula sete por cento

rules.rule: Expand units and notation into words.
rules.example: km -> quilômetros; km/s -> quilômetros por segundo; g/cm³ -> gramas por centímetro cúbico; 10⁴⁴ J -> dez elevado a quarenta e quatro joules

rules.rule: For acronyms, either expand them (URSS, EUA, ONU) or read them as one word with an accent for the stress (Otan, Onu, Ráf). Name a single letter in Portuguese.
rules.example: Dia D -> Dia Dê; H-alfa -> agá alfa
rules.why: Unspelled, 'Dia D' was read 'dia W'.

rules.rule: Speak a hyphen-number compound as two words.
rules.example: hélio-3 -> hélio três

rules.rule: Respell English loanwords in pt-BR orthography.
rules.example: tag -> tégui; Lend-Lease -> Lend-Lís

rules.rule: Apply loanword respellings to whole words, not substrings.
rules.example: ' tag' -> ' tégui' would also turn 'tags' into 'téguis' and 'tagarela' into 'téguiarela'
rules.why: sem-parar's spoken() uses str.replace on ' tag'. It is latent: the current cue sheet has only 'tag' and 'tag.' (inferred).

rules.rule: A mid-line ellipsis becomes a full stop in the spoken text (Piper). A trailing ellipsis is left as is.
rules.example: 'Então... vai' -> 'Então. Vai'; 'Senhoras e senhores...' unchanged
rules.why: The pause comes from Piper's --sentence-silence.

rules.rule: Do not speak a parenthetical acronym after its expansion.
rules.example: Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) -> Organização das Nações Unidas

rules.rule: Condense the narration when the caption sentence is longer than its shot allows at a natural pace.
rules.example: NARR: condensed lines per caption group

rules.rule: In shorts, put years on screen only and keep lines short.
rules.example: 'Setembro: a Alemanha invade a Polônia.' (the year is in the title)
rules.why: The first cut ran up to 8 syllables/s with full years inside 4 s shots.

rules.rule: Pace: calm pt-BR is 5-5.5 syllables/s. Take selection aims at 5.3. Ease lines above 6.0 toward 5.6 (at most 15 % slower). vo_qa flags above 6.2. Never compress (VO_MAX_STRETCH 1.0 in shorts).
rules.example: v007 Short final: 4.9-6.0 syll/s; v004 Short: 5.3-5.7
rules.why: Chatterbox's pt delivery runs 6-8 syllables/s whatever the settings. cfg_weight 0.3 gives a slower, more deliberate delivery.

rules.rule: Count syllables as vowel groups after stripping accents; Portuguese is close to one syllable per vowel group.
rules.example: syllables(): NFKD, strip combining marks, count [aeiouy]+

rules.rule: Cut each Chatterbox take at Whisper's first and last word (0.15 s before, 0.25 s after), not by level.
rules.example: HEAD, TAIL = 0.15, 0.25
rules.why: Chatterbox runs on after the sentence with breaths and mumbles that Whisper does not transcribe.

rules.rule: Lines must not overlap and must end before their cut. The builder errors when a line starts less than 0.1 s after the previous one ends. vo_qa flags a gap under 0.15 s or a line running more than 0.15 s past a cut.
On screen, use pt-BR locale formats.
Piper fitting: try shorter length-scales before giving up the window, and start the line a little after its caption appears.
rules.example: v002: scale 1.0 down to 0.88 in 0.04 steps, LEAD 0.4 s, MARGIN 0.3 s; v007 Piper: 1.0/0.95/0.91/0.87
rules.why: Historical (Piper is no longer used).

rules.rule: Abbreviations never carry periods in the spoken text; write them out.
rules.example: Sr. -> senhor; Dra. -> doutora; etc. -> et cétera; p.ex. -> por exemplo
rules.why: the sentence splitter breaks at a period followed by a space

rules.rule: Run vo.hazards on every spoken line before synthesis, then have a person listen to the opening line.

Whisper cannot verify letter names: a respelled acronym (á bê cê, pê tê) is heard back as the bare letters or a different word, so the word-error check passes or fails for the wrong reason. Approve a letter-name respelling by listening, and record who listened and when in the entry's source.
rules.example: ABC -> á bê cê (elevenlabs): approved by ear 2026-10-07; the Whisper transcript of the take cannot confirm it
rules.why: observed on the Lula 3.0.0 film: eleven acronyms were respelled and approved by the owner's ear because the transcript could not tell the readings apart.
